title: Arrays: Ordered Storage in a Row
lead: An array stores items side-by-side in memory. Because each slot is the same size, finding any element takes the same time no matter how big the array is.

sections.heading: The core idea
sections.body: Imagine a row of labelled mailboxes. Box 0, box 1, box 2… You jump straight to box 5 without opening the others. That instant access (O(1)) is what makes arrays powerful for reading data.

sections.heading: The trade-off
sections.body: Insertion in the middle is slow — every element after the insertion point must shift one step. If you insert at position 2 in an array of 1000 elements, 998 items move. For heavy insertion workloads, consider a linked list instead.

tryThis: Declare an array of 5 numbers. Access the last element using its index. Now insert a value at position 1 and count how many items had to move.
